quiz.q: Why do Indian states face a severe vertical financial imbalance according to the constitutional scheme?
options: Their social expenditure responsibilities are high while their revenue sources are rigid and low-yielding.
They are completely prohibited from receiving any statutory grants or shares from central tax revenues.
They must surrender all locally collected tax receipts directly into the Union Consolidated Fund.
Their borrowing powers allow unlimited foreign commercial loans without any domestic market regulation.
quiz.why: States bear heavy social spending commitments while their assigned taxes are rigid and low-yielding, creating a vertical imbalance.

quiz.q: What constitutional innovation did Article 246A introduce to Indian fiscal federalism under the 101st Amendment?
options: It transferred all indirect taxation powers exclusively to the Union Parliament.
It granted concurrent powers to Parliament and state legislatures to tax goods and services.
It abolished all state sales taxes without creating any replacement legislative mechanism.
It placed the Union List completely beyond the constitutional scope of GST legislation.
quiz.why: Article 246A established concurrent legislative powers, allowing Parliament and state assemblies to tax goods and services simultaneously.

quiz.q: How do Finance Commission recommendations differ from the discretionary transfers historically made by the Planning Commission?
options: Finance Commission transfers are executive decrees, whereas Planning Commission transfers were mandated by constitutional statute.
Finance Commission transfers require equal state representation, whereas Planning Commission bodies included only state chief ministers.
Finance Commission transfers represent constitutional statutory devolution, whereas Planning Commission grants were centralized and discretionary.
Finance Commission transfers apply exclusively to centrally sponsored schemes, whereas Planning Commission grants covered divisible pool taxes.
quiz.why: Grants recommended by the constitutional Finance Commission are statutory, unlike the centralized discretionary transfers historically made by the Planning Commission.

quiz.q: What is a key institutional rule governing the functioning and meetings of the GST Council under Article 279A?
options: Decisions can only be ratified if all participating state finance ministers reach unanimous agreement.
The Union Finance Minister possesses absolute unilateral veto power over any convened council quorum.
Meetings require a minimum quorum of two-thirds of the total membership to conduct business.
A valid meeting requires a quorum consisting of at least half of the total council members.
quiz.why: Under Article 279A, the GST Council requires a quorum of half of its total members to conduct valid proceedings.
